results.claim: The constructive branch of the recorded target is equivalent to exhibiting a reachable-state class C of one-key binary trees that contains the empty state, consists entirely of WSTs, is closed under dictionary insertion and deletion, and has deterministic search and complete update algorithms taking O(log(n+2)) worst-case time; the target does not require accepting every arbitrary Definition-1 WST as an initial state.
results.proof_sketch: Given any data structure meeting the target, let C be the representations reachable from its empty initialization under its operations. Then C has every listed property, so the intermediate statement is necessary for a constructive solution. Conversely, such a class C together with its algorithms is itself a WST data structure: initialization selects its empty member, closure makes every update and its rebalancing valid, the WST condition holds after every operation, and the stated operation bounds transfer unchanged. The recorded target asks for a data structure, not an updater whose input is every binary tree satisfying Definition 1. Thus this reachable-class statement is the exact structural reformulation needed for the constructive disjunct.

results.claim: Every valid 2–3 search tree has an explicit one-key-per-binary-node encoding E that is a WST; whenever a two-key macro-node occurs, E is not a strict BST.
results.proof_sketch: For a one-key macro-node [a] with ordered children C0,C1, use binary node a with children E(C0),E(C1). For [a<b] with ordered children C0,C1,C2, use binary root a, right child E(C2), and a left continuation node b whose children are E(C0),E(C1). Induct on macro-height. At a one-key node, C0<a<C1 implies C0<C1, the WST split. At continuation b, C0<C1. At the two-key root a, every key in {b}∪C0∪C1 is below every key of C2. Child encodings satisfy WST inductively, and empty comparisons are vacuous. Each physical node stores exactly one key. If [a<b] occurs, b>a is a left child of a, violating the strict BST invariant.

results.claim: The macro-node boundaries and search branches of E are recognizable in O(1) time per macro level using only keys and child pointers.
results.proof_sketch: At the encoding root a of a one-key macro-node, the left pointer is null at a leaf or enters E(C0), whose root key is below a. At a two-key macro-node, the left pointer is the continuation b>a. A null test and at most one key comparison therefore identify arity without a tag. In the one-key case, comparison with a selects C0 or C1 or finds a. In the two-key case, comparisons with a and b select C0,C1,C2 or find a stored key. The required child pointers are respectively (a.left,a.right) or (b.left,b.right,a.right), so routing costs O(1) per macro level.

results.claim: Standard 2–3-tree insertion transfers to E and preserves the encoded class with O(1) work at every visited macro level, including every split and root-growth case.
results.proof_sketch: Descend using the decoded interval branch. A one-key leaf absorbs the new distinct key and becomes a sorted two-key leaf. A two-key leaf plus the new key gives x<y<z; replace the overflow by [x] and [z] and promote y. A promotion into a one-key parent is absorbed, producing a two-key node with three ordered children. A promotion into a two-key parent produces three ordered keys and four ordered child intervals; split around the middle key into the two outer one-key nodes and promote the middle key. The promotion can arrive in the left, middle, or right position, which these ordered cases cover. A promotion from the old root creates a new one-key root. Each rewrite touches constantly many keys and pointers, preserves ordered intervals and common leaf depth, and propagates at most one split upward. Re-encoding the changed macro-nodes therefore remains in E and remains a WST.

results.claim: Standard 2–3-tree deletion transfers to E and preserves the encoded class with O(1) work at every visited macro level, including internal replacement, every borrow and merge orientation, and root contraction.
results.proof_sketch: For an internal key, replace it by the predecessor from its immediately lower child interval and delete that predecessor at a leaf; interval order is preserved. A two-key leaf can lose one key directly. Removing a one-key leaf's key creates one zero-key underflow. If either adjacent sibling has two keys, move the intervening parent separator down, move the sibling's adjacent boundary key up, and transfer its adjacent child when internal. Otherwise each adjacent sibling has one key, so merge the underflow, one adjacent sibling, and their separator into one two-key node. A merge removes one parent key: a two-key parent becomes one-key, while a one-key nonroot parent underflows and propagates the single deficit upward. Left/right siblings and both sides of a middle child exhaust the orientations. An empty root contracts to its unique child or the empty tree. Every repair is constant-size and preserves interval order and equal leaf depth; re-encoding preserves WST.

results.claim: An encoded 2–3 tree with n keys has binary height O(log(n+2)), and its search, insertion, deletion, and all associated rebalancing take deterministic O(log(n+2)) worst-case time.
results.proof_sketch: For macro-height H in edges, the minimum nonempty key count satisfies N(0)=1 and N(H)=1+2N(H−1), hence N(H)=2^(H+1)−1 and H=O(log(n+2)). Each macro-node contributes at most two physical binary nodes along a path, so binary height is at most 2H+1. Search does constant work per macro level. Insertion performs one descent and propagates at most one constant-size split per level. Deletion performs the search and, only for an internal key, one predecessor descent, followed by at most one constant-size borrow or merge per level. Root growth and contraction are constant work. Therefore all costs, including rebalancing, are deterministic worst-case logarithmic rather than expected or amortized.

results.claim: The encoded 2–3 reachable-state class satisfies the structural reformulation and therefore fully resolves the recorded target, with reachable states that are genuinely WST rather than strict BST states.
results.proof_sketch: Let C consist of the empty tree and encodings E(T) of valid 2–3 search trees. The encoding claim puts every member of C in Definition 1. The decoder supplies search; the insertion and deletion claims give closure under every update and include all rebalancing; the height claim gives the requested deterministic worst-case bound. Thus every condition of the equivalent reachable-class statement holds and transfers back to the target. Moreover, inserting 1 and then 2 reaches the two-key leaf [1<2], encoded as root 1 with left child 2. It is a WST because its right subtree is empty, but it is not a strict BST. Hence the resolution does not rely solely on treating an ordinary BST as a WST.

results.claim: Independently, under the recorded definition an AVL search tree is a WST supporting every insertion and deletion, including rebalancing, in deterministic O(log(n+2)) worst-case time.
results.proof_sketch: At every node, the strict BST invariant gives each left key < node key < each right key, hence every left key is below every right key as Definition 1 requires. Standard AVL search, insertion, successor-based deletion, and single/double rotations preserve BST order. Bottom-up repair does constant work at each visited ancestor and restores child-height difference at most one; the usual single- and double-rotation height case analysis covers both imbalance orientations. If M(h) is the minimum number of nodes at AVL height h, M(h)=1+M(h−1)+M(h−2), so M(h) grows exponentially and h=O(log(n+2)). Thus this is also a literal witness, although the encoded 2–3 construction above additionally reaches non-BST states.

results.claim: The encoded class is a proper subclass of all balanced WSTs, but coverage of arbitrary externally supplied WST states is a strictly stronger requirement than the recorded target and does not weaken the full resolution.
results.proof_sketch: The balanced binary tree with root 2, left leaf 3, and right leaf 4 satisfies Definition 1 because 3<4, yet it is not a valid encoding: the left child 3>2 would be parsed as a continuation of a two-key macro-node, but that putative macro-node has only its C2 child and lacks C0,C1. Thus Definition 1 alone does not imply the macro parse, ordered macro intervals, or equal macro-leaf depth. The first result proves that a data structure needs closure only for its own reachable states. Consequently no conversion or update algorithm for this arbitrary witness is needed to meet the recorded existential target.

results.claim: For a WST in the standard right-rotation configuration z(left=y(A,B), right=D), the unmodified rotation is a WST exactly when A is empty or every key of A is smaller than key(z); symmetrically, a left rotation at z is safe exactly when D is empty or key(z) is smaller than every key of D.
results.proof_sketch: Before the right rotation, WST gives A<B at y and {key(y)}∪A∪B<D at z whenever both compared subtrees are nonempty. Afterwards, z has children B,D, so B<D is inherited. The new root y has left subtree A and right subtree {key(z)}∪B∪D. Its A<B and A<D obligations are inherited, leaving exactly A<key(z) as the only new condition. This is necessary and sufficient, with empty A vacuous; empty B or D removes rather than adds obligations. Mirroring the calculation for a left rotation leaves exactly key(z)<D.

results.claim: There is a three-node WST on which an ordinary right rotation destroys the WST invariant.
results.proof_sketch: Take root z=1, its left child y=3, and y's left child 2, with all other children null. Initially every internal right subtree is empty, so all left-versus-right requirements are vacuous and the tree is a WST. The right rotation makes y the root with left leaf 2 and right leaf z=1. Definition 1 at the new root requires 2<1, which is false.

results.claim: A three-node WST shows more strongly that permuting only the two pivot keys cannot universally repair a right rotation; a repair retaining the rotated topology may have to touch the transferred subtree.
results.proof_sketch: Take z=1, y=2, and A as the leaf 3, with B,D empty. The pre-state is a WST. In the rotated topology A remains the left leaf, while the right leaf receives one of the pivot keys 1 or 2 under either pivot-only permutation. The root split then requires 3<1 or 3<2, so neither assignment works. The same three-node topology can be made a WST by labeling root, left, right as 1,2,3, respectively, but this necessarily moves A's key.

results.claim: The maximum key of a nonempty WST subtree lies among the node keys on the path that follows a nonempty right child and otherwise the left child; in a perfect height-h WST, the h+1 node keys on the right spine can be mutually order-unconstrained by the WST invariant.
results.proof_sketch: If a right subtree exists, every left-subtree key is below every right-subtree key, so the maximum is the current node key or lies in the right subtree; recurse right. Without a right subtree, only the current node and left subtree remain; recurse left. This proves the path claim by induction. For a perfect tree, recursively assign every off-spine left block a disjoint interval below the corresponding right block, while placing all right-spine node keys in one common higher interval. Each WST split remains true under every permutation of those spine keys: a node's own key is excluded from its split, and ancestor splits place the candidates on the same side. Hence their mutual order is unconstrained.

results.claim: In the unaugmented comparison model with only keys and child pointers, for every h>=1 there is an n=2^(h+2)−1 WST at an AVL left-left imbalance for which testing the ordinary rotation, and any key-permutation repair retaining the rotated topology, requires Ω(h)=Ω(log n) comparisons in the worst case.
results.proof_sketch: Let A be perfect of height h and B,D perfect of height h−1 in z(left=y(A,B),right=D). Then n=(2^(h+1)−1)+2(2^h−1)+2=2^(h+2)−1; z has imbalance two and every proper subtree is height-balanced. Arrange ordered blocks so the input is a WST and the h+1 independent candidates from A's path are its only possible keys above a threshold key(z). By the rotation criterion, legality is the conjunction that all candidates are below key(z), whose comparison certificate needs Ω(h) comparisons. For repair, let m=|A|, put the two pivot keys below all m A-keys, and put the m−1 keys of B∪D above them in WST-compatible blocks. The rotated root has two m-node child blocks. Whatever key occupies the root, a valid root split forces the left block to be the m smallest remaining keys. At most two A-keys can therefore be outside it, and they must include max(A). Reducing h+1 independent maximum candidates to a guaranteed set of at most two needs at least h−1 comparisons.

results.claim: The rotation lower bound is a precise limitation on one primitive and neither obstructs the encoded 2–3 construction nor weakens the full target resolution.
results.proof_sketch: The lower bound concerns unaugmented fixed-topology repair on a general WST. The encoded class instead carries a locally recognizable structural invariant and rebalances through constant-size 2–3 split, borrow, merge, growth, and contraction rewrites. It never invokes a universal repaired binary rotation. Moreover, even a constant number of Ω(log n) repairs could fit an O(log n) update, and the adversary gives no reduction from every update method to that primitive. The result therefore preserves the parent's genuine obstruction progress while remaining logically separate from the constructive target proof.

final_writeup:
Resolution: full for the recorded target.

The structural reformulation is this: the constructive branch is equivalent to finding a class C of reachable one-key binary representations that contains the empty state, consists of WSTs, is closed under insertion and deletion (including every repair), and supports deterministic worst-case logarithmic operations. Any data structure yields such a class by taking its reachable states. Conversely, such a class and its algorithms are a WST data structure with the same bounds. The target does not quantify over arbitrary preexisting trees satisfying Definition 1.

Use valid 2–3 search trees as the intermediate structure. A macro-node has either one key [a] and ordered children C0,C1, or two keys [a<b] and ordered children C0,C1,C2. Encode [a] as binary node a with children E(C0),E(C1). Encode [a<b] as binary root a whose right child is E(C2) and whose left child is a continuation node b with children E(C0),E(C1). Thus every physical binary node stores exactly one key.

The encoding is a WST by induction on macro-height. At [a], C0<a<C1 implies C0<C1. At continuation b, C0<C1. At the root of [a<b], every key in {b}∪C0∪C1 is below every key of C2. Those are precisely the required left-versus-right comparisons; the recursively encoded children satisfy them inductively. Empty comparisons are vacuous. Whenever a two-key macro-node occurs, the continuation b>a is a left child of a, so the encoding is not a strict BST.

The macro structure needs no tag or augmented field. At macro-root a, the left pointer is null at a one-key leaf or enters C0 with root key below a; for a two-key node it points to continuation b>a. One null test and one comparison identify the case. Comparisons with a and, when present, b then select the appropriate one of C0,C1,C2 in constant time per macro level.

Insertion is standard bottom-up 2–3 insertion. A one-key leaf absorbs a key. A three-key overflow x<y<z splits into [x] and [z] and promotes y. A one-key parent absorbs a promotion. A two-key parent plus a promotion has three ordered keys and four ordered child intervals, so it splits around the middle key and promotes that key. A root promotion creates a new root. The left, middle, and right promotion positions are all instances of this ordered case. Each rewrite changes only constantly many keys and pointers, preserves the child intervals and common leaf depth, and propagates at most one split per level.

For deletion, replace an internal key by its predecessor in the immediately lower child interval and delete at that leaf. A two-key leaf simply becomes one-key. If a one-key node underflows, borrow through the intervening separator from an adjacent two-key sibling, moving the sibling boundary key up and transferring the adjacent child when internal. If neither adjacent sibling has two keys, merge the underflow, a one-key sibling, and their separator into one two-key node. This can propagate only one underflow per level. The left/right and middle-child orientations exhaust the sibling cases. An empty root contracts to its unique child or to the empty tree. Every repair is constant-size and preserves interval order and equal leaf depth, hence its encoding remains a WST.

If H is macro-height in edges, the minimum key count is N(0)=1 and N(H)=1+2N(H−1)=2^(H+1)−1. Hence H=O(log(n+2)). A macro level contributes at most two physical nodes to a binary path. Search does constant work per level; insertion has one descent and one possible split per ancestor; deletion has at most a search and predecessor descent and one possible underflow repair per ancestor. Root changes are constant. All three operations, including rebalancing, therefore take deterministic O(log(n+2)) worst-case time.

Let C be the empty tree together with all these encodings. The preceding invariant, closure, and cost proofs establish every condition of the structural reformulation, so the conclusion transfers to the recorded target. The construction is genuinely non-BST: inserting 1 and 2 reaches [1<2], encoded as root 1 with left child 2. An AVL tree is also a literal WST witness because strict BST order implies Definition 1, but the 2–3 encoding shows that the resolution is not merely the BST special case.

The encoded family is a proper subclass of all WSTs. For example, root 2 with left leaf 3 and right leaf 4 is a balanced WST but has no valid encoded macro parse. That fact does not create a gap: accepting every externally supplied Definition-1 WST is stronger than the target's data-structure requirement.

The parent's rotation progress remains valid but is auxiliary. A right rotation z(left=y(A,B),right=D) preserves WST exactly when A is empty or A<key(z); the mirror left rotation requires key(z)<D. The chain 1(left=3(left=2)) is a three-node failure, and 1(left=2(left=3)) shows that swapping only the pivot keys cannot always repair the rotated topology. In perfect height-h WSTs, h+1 maximum candidates on a right spine can be mutually unordered, yielding Ω(h)=Ω(log n) comparisons for unaugmented fixed-topology rotation testing and key-permutation repair on an explicit AVL-imbalance family. This limits universal constant-time rotation repair, but it does not touch the encoded construction, whose balancing consists of constant-size macro rewrites.
